function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine plus points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Stop signs: Must come to a full stop and yield to traffic already in the intersection.
• Pedestrians: Must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to citations and points. | | **School Bus Laws** | • When a school bus stops and its red lights flash, all vehicles must stop.
• In Texas, the stop is required in both directions on two‑lane roads. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Drivers must signal before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle being overtaken is turning left. | Improper lane changes can lead to citations. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or stop sign.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | Violations can result in fines and towing. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing of vehicles without proper permits is illegal. | Failure to register can lead to a $100 fine. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | Points vary by offense severity. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Failure to maintain insurance can result in license suspension. | ### Quick Reference for Common Violations | Violation | Typical Fine | Points | |-----------|--------------|--------| | Speeding (1–10 mph over limit) | $50 | 1 | | Speeding (11–20 mph over limit) | $100 | 2 | | Speeding (21+ mph over limit) | $200 | 3 | | Seat‑belt non‑compliance | $50 | 1 | | Cell‑phone use | $50 | 1 | | DUI (BAC 0.08–0.15) | $500–$1,000 | 3–4 | | DUI (BAC > 0.15) | $1,000–$2,000 | 4–5 | ### Resources - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official traffic law updates and driver handbook. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text. - **Texas Driver Handbook** – Practical guide for drivers. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
